title: Ephesians
summary: Ephesians is a biblical book focused on union with Christ, grace, Jew-Gentile unity, church identity, holiness, and spiritual conflict.
historical_context: Ephesians presents God's cosmic purpose in Christ and the church's unified life in grace.
ancient_near_east_context: Ephesians belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Ephesians should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Ephesians as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Pauline Epistles, book 5 of 13, Ephesians contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting union with Christ, grace, Jew-Gentile unity, church identity, holiness, and spiritual conflict to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Ephesians as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Ephesians uses epistle within Pauline Epistles, book 5 of 13 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Ephesians helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional Pauline authorship or Pauline circle attribution
Critical scholarship debates several letters and recognizes co-workers in some correspondence
date_ranges: Some disputed letters are placed later or in the Pauline school
original_audience: Mixed Jewish-Gentile congregations and church leaders across the Roman world
historical_setting: The Greco-Roman world of mission, patronage, and local house churches
canonical_role: Ephesians anchors union with Christ, grace, Jew-Gentile unity, church identity, holiness, and spiritual conflict within Pauline Epistles, book 5 of 13 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How doctrine, ethics, and pastoral counsel fit together

related_objects.notes: Paul frames the letter's prayer and teaching.
Grace is central to the letter's salvation language.
Union with Christ shapes the letter's theology.
The church is described as a unified people in Christ.
Gifts build up the body toward maturity.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Ephesians first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
The relationship links on Ephesians are orientation anchors, not a full interpretive outline of the book.
